steps.body: Volume is a count: each unit cube fills one unit of space, so the number of cubes that pack a solid IS its volume.
steps.narration: Volume is a count: each unit cube fills one unit of space, so the number of cubes that pack a solid IS its volume.

widget.prompt: Build the base layer of a solid: a 5-by-4 rectangle of unit cubes.
widget.successFeedback: 20 cubes in the base layer — and the volume will be that count repeated for every layer.
widget.lowFeedback: Smaller than 20 — keep building until the layer reaches 5 by 4.
widget.highFeedback: Larger than 20 — a side has grown past the dimensions given.
widget.factorFeedback: That area is right, but from different sides — this layer must measure 5 across and 4 deep.

options.label: Yes — a cube is one unit of space

predict.reveal: The formula is a shortcut for the count; the count is what volume means.

cml.actionGoal: Build one layer, then count how many layers the height stacks for g5v count cubes.
invariants: Volume is a count of unit cubes, and a prism organises that count into identical layers: the base area counts one layer and the height counts the layers, which is why g5v count cubes is a product rather than a sum.
misconceptions: Adding the three dimensions instead of multiplying, stopping at the base area, or adding a removed notch instead of subtracting it.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the height doubled but the base stayed the same, what would happen to the cube count?

widget.prompt: Why does counting unit cubes measure volume? Choose a new reason.

options.label: Each unit cube fills one unit of space
options.feedback: Correct — volume is a count of equal units, exactly as area counts equal squares.

options.label: Because cubes are easy to draw
options.feedback: Convenience is not the reason; the cube being one unit of space is.

options.label: Because cubes have six faces
options.feedback: Face count describes the shape's surface, which is a different measurement entirely.

options.label: It does not — volume needs a formula
options.feedback: The formula is a shortcut for the count, not a replacement for what volume means.

steps.body: This is the same idea as area, one dimension further on. Area counts equal squares covering a surface; volume counts equal cubes filling a space.
steps.narration: This is the same idea as area, one dimension further on. Area counts equal squares covering a surface; volume counts equal cubes filling a space.

widget.prompt: Build a new base layer: make a 3-by-6 rectangle of unit cubes.
widget.successFeedback: 18 cubes fill this one layer. Repeating that complete layer creates a volume.
widget.lowFeedback: That is fewer than 18 cubes. Build until the base is 3 by 6.
widget.highFeedback: That is more than 18 cubes. Keep the base at 3 by 6.
widget.factorFeedback: That area is correct from another pair of factors, but this base must be 3 across and 6 deep.

widget.prompt: Compute 6 × 7 — the base area of a 6-by-7 rectangle, in square units. Calculate this fresh case.

commonErrors.feedback: Adding gives the distance round part of the edge, not the number of squares covering the base.
That is the perimeter of the base; area counts the squares inside it.
